To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the liver is a major site for synthesis of TAG from both dietary carbohydrate and fat, and the TAG synthesized from dietary carbohydrate in the liver is mostly transported to adipocytes, and that the incorporation of labeled glucose into total lipoids and TAG in adipose tissue was very low, while that of acetate was much higher.

dietary fat suppresses the incorporation of labeled glucose into lipids in liver, while the incorporation is enhanced in adipose tissue, and that TAG synthesized from acetates and glucose in the livers is transported to the adipose tissue.
dietary carbohydrate and fat affect the incorporation of glucose and acetate into lipids in rat liver and adipose tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of acetate and the metabolism of glucose in the liver and in adipose tissue.
the incorporation of acetate and of glucose into lipids in liver and adipose tissues after intravenous injections of labeled substrates.
the metabolism of acetate and its relation to glucose in the liver and epididymale adipose tissue of rats fed fat-free and fat-containing diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incorporation of acetate and/or glucose into total lipides and TAG is more greatly suppressed in the liver and the adipose tissue by dietary corn oil, and that the incorporation of glucose into total lipid and TAG is more suppressed in the liver by dietary corn oil.
TAG in the liver is mostly derived from dietary fat, but TAG in adipose tissue is derived from dietary fat and acetate.
the dietary fat is the main source for TAG synthesis in the liver and its transport to the adipose tissue, and the dietary carbohydrate is not a major source for TAG synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dietary fat, especially saturated fat, would be more important for lipid metabolism than dietary carbohydrate.
dietary carbohydrate is more greatly suppressed than dietary fat for the TAG synthesis from glucose in liver and adipose tissues.
TAG in adipose tissue was mostly derived from dietary fat, but that TAG from glucose was also present in the adipose tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver and adipocyte are the major sites of lipid synthesis, but the liver is the major site of TAG production.
dietary carbohydrate is less likely to be converted to TAG in the liver than is dietary fat, because TAG synthesized from dietary carbohydrate is mostly transported to adipocytes.
the incorporation of acetate and/or glucose into TAG in adipose tissue is not as high as in the liver, but the TAG in adipose tissues are derived from acetate and/or from glucose in the liver.
